title: B.A. in Anthropology
description: Students are required to complete a minimum of 69 units of courses as follows:

subsections.title: Any three courses from
text: ANTH1020# (recommended), ARTS1005, 1009, 1010, BMBL1001, CHES1101 or 1102, CHLL1900 or 1902 or 1903, CURE1000, 1110, 1400 [CUMT1000], ENGE1000, FAAS1900, HIST1000 or 1700 or 1701, JASP1090, LING1000, MUSC1000, PHIL1110, THEO1000, TRAN1000

subsections.title: Research components (field project I and II)

text: Nine courses from (a) and/or (b) below, with at least four courses from (b) Ethnography and Area Studies

notes.text: ANTH courses at 2000 and above level as well as those labeled as # will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.

Up to four related courses (12 units) offered by the Department of History and the Department of Japanese Studies or up to three related courses (9 units) offered by other Departments or Programmes (undergraduate or postgraduate) as approved by this Department may be recognized as courses for fulfillment of major programme requirement.
Old course code used in 2024-25 and before.
Old course code used in 2025-26 and before.

subsections.title: Voluntary Concentrations
text: Students are encouraged to choose one, or up to two concentrations by taking the relevant courses in fulfillment of the Major Programme requirement listed above. Students will be required to complete a minimum of five courses designated to the concentration of their choice. (Other courses may also be recognized as fulfillment of concentration requirement with the approval of the Department.) The six concentrations are as follows:

parts.description: Students are required to complete a minimum of 60 units of courses as follows:

subsections.title: Nine courses from (a) and/or (b) below, with at least three courses from (b) Ethnography and Area Studies

notes.text: ANTH courses at 2000 and above level as well as those labeled as # will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.

Up to three related courses (9 units) offered by other Departments or Programmes (undergraduate or postgraduate) as approved by this Department may be recognized as courses for fulfillment of major programme requirement.

Subject to the Department’s prior approval, students are allowed to take both ANTH4300 and 4301 in the same term in their final year of study after finishing a one-year or one-term exchange programme.
